| ChatGPT | `plugin.json`, `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`; `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` for workspace import | `skills` path | Detect native tools in the current session; general-purpose agent reads the persona |
| omp | `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` (Claude-compatible fallback) | `skills/` (default) | Personas from `agents/`/`.claude-plugin/agents/` register as native `task` agents |
| Muse | `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` (Claude-compatible fallback) | `skills/` (default) | 10 adapters import as agents; tool projections unsupported |

Persona prompts live in `agents/`, the directory Antigravity
scans for subagents. Each persona has `name` and `description` frontmatter, so
harnesses that load `agents/*.md` register them as named subagents
(`egm-design`, `egm-zoom-out`, and so on).

When you add a reviewer persona, add a Claude adapter under
`.claude-plugin/agents/` and list it in `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`.
The adapter reads the shared persona and sets Claude's read-only tools and
context isolation. This avoids imposing Claude tool names on other hosts.
In Claude Code, `/plugin` > Errors will report that the default `agents/` folder is ignored because the manifest sets `"agents"`; this warning is expected and harmless (see [Claude integration](claude.md#claude-code-warning-default-agents-folder-is-ignored)).

## Delegation

Skills say "spawn a subagent" and name a persona. Each harness maps that
phrase to its own tool:

| Harness | Subagent tool | Named personas | Nesting |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Antigravity | `invoke_subagent` | Yes | Yes |
| Claude Code | Agent (Task) tool | Yes | Up to 3 levels by default |
| Claude Cowork | Cowork subagents | Yes | Subagents run inside Cowork |
| Codex | Native spawn/wait tools; inspect the available schema | No | Detect at runtime; direct dispatch fallback |
| ChatGPT | Native spawn/wait tools when exposed by the current Work session | No | Detect at runtime; direct dispatch fallback |
| omp | `task` tool | Yes | Yes |
| Muse | Native subagents; inspect the available schema | Named spawn rejected in 1.4.14; general-purpose fallback verified | Detect at runtime; direct dispatch fallback |

Where a harness has no named persona, the skill spawns a general-purpose
subagent and tells it to read `agents/<file>.md` first. If a harness cannot
nest subagents, use direct dispatch instead of the synthesizer.

A Goldfish review needs a fresh context. If a harness has no subagent tool,
the review skills stop instead of running in the same context. Check actual
tool availability rather than inferring it from the product name. This applies
to standalone Antigravity IDE and to ChatGPT modes that do not expose native
fresh-context delegation.

Fresh conversation context does not mean that the host omits its instruction
files. Codex's `fork_context: false` and `fork_turns: "none"` isolate parent
turns; they do not establish that project or user instructions are excluded.
Keep stable workspace conventions in instruction files. State review
assumptions that the Goldfish must challenge as explicit review criteria.

## Artifact Directory

Skills write briefs, drafts, and reports to the working directory, or to the
harness's artifact directory if it has one. In Claude Code, Claude Cowork,
Codex, and ChatGPT, you can name another folder. Add this line to your prompt,
or to an agent instructions file that your harness loads (`CLAUDE.md` or
`AGENTS.md`, in the project or at user level):

```text
EGM artifact directory: .dev/docs
```

A relative path is relative to the working directory. If a path set in an
instructions file resolves outside the working directory, after following
symbolic links, EGM asks you to confirm it before creating the folder or
writing there. If you decline or no one can confirm, as in a headless run, the
files go to the working directory. The answer isn't saved, so a new session
asks again. A path in your prompt needs no confirmation. Design docs and other
project files do not move. Claude Code reads a project `AGENTS.md` only when
the project has no `CLAUDE.md`.

Commit approved specifications in `docs/designs/` and project rules in
`AGENTS.md`. Teammates and agents then use the same committed files. Add
`.dev/docs` to `.gitignore` only to keep scratch drafts out of git before
approval.

**Antigravity CLI**, **Claude Code**, and **Codex** pass automated installation
and end-to-end workflow fixtures. Reviewer isolation evidence is narrower:
parent-turn isolation and host-instruction exclusion are separate results.

Claude reviewer adapters set `omitClaudeMd: true`; see the

The Codex test and recorded Antigravity run check parent-turn isolation only;
neither verifies instruction-file exclusion. No host-specific exclusion

**Claude Cowork** ([#105](https://github.com/google/elephant-goldfish-model/issues/105)) and **ChatGPT Work** ([#106](https://github.com/google/elephant-goldfish-model/issues/106)) have working installation paths with open cloud trace verification gaps. # FULL_SNAPSHOT safety contract under review

Author: Alex Callow  
Issue: GLO-34, Define the FULL_SNAPSHOT safety contract  
Status: Working hypothesis for Goldfish review

## Purpose

DELTA can update rows supplied by an operator. FULL_SNAPSHOT adds versioned retirement for frames that the upstream source confirmed were withdrawn. It also needs to handle frames that leave one region and appear in another, out-of-order exports, and competing manual edits. The exercise can run this locally with a controlled exporter and a dataset separate from the app inventory. A real rollout depends on an authoritative upstream producer.

## Export evidence

A trusted exporter reads one complete, consistent source scope. Its signed manifest identifies the canonical scope, UTC capture time, expected logical record count from the source read, and SHA-256 checksum of the CSV. The importer verifies the producer, signed fields, row count, and exact bytes of the pinned S3 object version before inventory writes. The manifest capture time is the watermark. The draft scopes are GLOBAL, country, country/region, and country/region/environment. An environment requires a country and a region.

The manifest also carries known lifecycle events. A move identifies the frame ID, origin and destination. A withdrawal identifies the frame ID, last known scope, and effective time. A reinstatement identifies the frame ID, destination scope, and effective time. The producer signs those claims with the snapshot. A real source must be able to establish scope completeness and these lifecycle events.

## Snapshot admission and ordering

Reject capture times in the future, and reject snapshots older than 24 hours. Check age at manifest verification and again before apply against the backend UTC clock. A job that ages out in the queue fails with SNAPSHOT_TOO_OLD. A rejected snapshot leaves inventory and the watermark unchanged.

For the same scope and capture time, identical signed contents and matching CSV bytes return the previous result without creating versions. Different signed contents at the same capture time are a conflict. Leave the previous result in place, identify its job, and require a fresh capture. Apply the original design's scope hierarchy for ordered watermarks. Reject a narrower snapshot older than a committed ancestor. Protect a newer descendant scope from retirement by a broader snapshot. Present rows still follow normal conflict checks under the original broader-snapshot rule.

## Scope validation and lifecycle behavior

A row outside the signed scope or with a malformed field needed to verify its scope fails the snapshot. A row with no recoverable frame ID also fails the snapshot. An identifiable row with a malformed field unrelated to scope protects that frame from retirement and counts toward the 5% malformed-row limit. A header-only or unrecoverable file failure leaves inventory and the watermark unchanged.

When an origin snapshot arrives before the destination, a signed move keeps the frame active at its last known location and reports that the destination import is pending. When the destination snapshot applies the move, append a new active version in that scope. Arrival in the reverse order must yield the same active frame and no intermediate retirement. An unexplained absence keeps the frame active and is shown in diagnostics.

Automatic retirement requires a signed withdrawal effective by the capture time. Protect a frame with a newer edit or move. Reject a snapshot that includes both a live row and a withdrawal for one frame. Retirement appends a RETIRED version with the withdrawal and job lineage. Retired frames remain visible through explicit filtering, direct lookup, and history. Ordinary edit and delete requests reject a snapshot-retired frame.

Reactivation requires a valid row in the destination scope and a signed reinstatement effective after the withdrawal and by the capture time. Protect newer manual actions. Append a new active version even when the row's details are unchanged. The existing DELTA force-overwrite rule still applies to manually deleted frames.

## Apply boundaries

Stage and validate the file outside the inventory lock. Recheck scope, lifecycle ordering and retirement eligibility against the protected pre-apply view. Use a single transaction to commit inventory versions, the job result, and the scope watermark. Before writing, reject if malformed rows exceed 5% or eligible retirements exceed the smaller of 100 frames and 10% of all pre-apply active frames in scope. Active means a current version in LIVE, PENDING, MAINTENANCE, BLOCKED, or DRAFT. The same set defines retirement eligibility. Manually deleted frames have no current version.

Wait at most 1 second to acquire the exclusive inventory lock. Let the worker retry contention within the freshness limit. Once the lock is acquired, allow at most 5 seconds for the full apply and roll back on timeout. Benchmark with a 10,000-row snapshot and competing manual writes before rollout. The existing 10 MiB and 10,000-row CSV limits apply.

## Verification examples

- Seed 100 frames in the app and issue three upstream withdrawals. A complete 97-row export retires exactly those three. Truncate that same export and check that the importer rejects it before inventory changes.
- Import Region A before B, then repeat on clean data with B first. Both orders end with the frame active in B and no intermediate RETIRED version.
- Submit an exact replay, a same-time conflict, an old or future capture, an unscopable row, a live row contradicting a withdrawal, and a reinstatement with an unchanged valid row.
- Exercise guard boundaries, the lock wait and apply deadlines, and rollback before advancing the watermark. Verify DELTA behavior and version history.
EOF

# FULL_SNAPSHOT safety contract and Goldfish review

**Author** — Alex Callow  
**Date** — 2026-11-27  
**Status** — Reviewed working contract. Open decisions are identified below.  
**Scope** — [GLO-34](https://linear.app/upfrontbeats/issue/GLO-34/define-the-full-snapshot-safety-contract) · [Contract reviewed](snapshot-contract.md)

## Overview

FULL_SNAPSHOT lets the app retire a frame after the source confirms its withdrawal. Operators should be able to see why it retired, which snapshot applied the change, and whether a later source event restored it. The local exercise can use a controlled exporter backed by data separate from the app inventory. A real rollout needs a producer that can make the same completeness and lifecycle claims for real inventory.

## Goals and non-goals

- Preserve one active frame and consistent version history when regional imports arrive in either order.
- Require verified source evidence for moves, withdrawals, and reinstatements. Keep unexplained absences visible for review.
- Keep apply atomic and bounded. A failed apply leaves inventory and the scope watermark unchanged.
- Keep deployed identity and permissions in [GLO-28](https://linear.app/upfrontbeats/issue/GLO-28/define-and-implement-import-authorization). GLO-34 defines the contract. [GLO-33](https://linear.app/upfrontbeats/issue/GLO-33/implement-scoped-snapshot-retirement-and-rollout-checks) implements and verifies it.

## Agreed contract

| Area | Decision |
| --- | --- |
| Export | A trusted producer reads a complete scope at a consistent point in time. Its signed manifest binds the scope, UTC capture time, expected logical row count and SHA-256 checksum to the pinned CSV bytes. The signature and evidence are checked before inventory writes. |
| Freshness | Reject future captures and new apply attempts older than 24 hours. Check age at manifest verification and again before apply. |
| Same-scope ordering | Return the original result for identical signed contents and CSV bytes. Reject different contents at the same capture time and identify the earlier job. A correction needs a fresh capture. |
| Scope and malformed data | Reject the whole snapshot for out-of-scope rows, an unverifiable required scope field, a missing recoverable frame ID, or an unrecoverable parse error. An identifiable malformed row with verified scope still counts as present. The job fails if more than 5% of logical data records are malformed. |
| Moves | Signed move evidence protects the frame when the origin snapshot arrives first. The valid destination row applies the move. Both arrival orders must end with the frame active in the destination and no intermediate retirement. |
| Withdrawal | Require a signed withdrawal effective by capture time. Protect newer edits or moves. Reject a live row paired with a withdrawal for the same frame. Unexplained absences remain active and show up in diagnostics. |
| Reinstatement | Require a signed reinstatement later than the withdrawal and effective by capture time, plus a valid row in the destination. A newer manual action takes precedence. Matching the old frame details is allowed. |
| Retired frames | Append a RETIRED version with withdrawal and job lineage. Expose it through direct lookup, history and an explicit retired filter. Ordinary edit and delete actions reject it. The existing force rule for manual deletion remains a separate case. |
| Apply limits | Use one transaction. Retire at most the lesser of 100 frames or 10% of pre-apply active frames in scope. Active means a current LIVE, PENDING, MAINTENANCE, BLOCKED, or DRAFT version. Wait at most 1 second for the exclusive inventory lock and allow 5 seconds for the whole apply once acquired. Benchmark a 10,000-row import with competing writes. |

## Analysis

### 1. Blocker — Order lifecycle events across scopes

A newer capture can repeat an older withdrawal. If a frame has already moved or been reinstated, the scope watermark and row timestamp do not tell us which lifecycle event is current. A newer manual edit can also occur after the withdrawal but before the capture. For example, a withdrawal effective at 09:00, a manual edit at 09:30, and a capture at 10:00 give different outcomes depending on the timestamp used.

The reviewers propose a stable signed event ID, an effective time, and a producer-issued sequence that increases per frame across all scopes. Store the accepted order with durable lineage and require the destination export to carry the same move evidence. Specify which scopes can attest to each event, and resolve equal or conflicting event sequences. Decide how source events compare with manual edits and the history of manual deletions. [Reviewed rules](snapshot-contract.md#scope-validation-and-lifecycle-behavior)

The existing hierarchy orders overlapping captures but protects a newer descendant primarily from retirement. Define what an older broad snapshot may do with a present row when either its current scope or destination has newer evidence. Also define equal-time overlap across different scopes. A stale ancestor row must not undo a newer move, withdrawal, or reinstatement. [Earlier hierarchy design](/Users/alexcallow/Sites/frame-inventory-exercise-main/docs/designs/bulk-csv-inventory-import-design.md:63)

### 2. Blocker — Preserve the retirement rules across every write path

Today DELTA compares source timestamps and payload hashes, and ordinary frame edits and deletes check the current version ID. Both paths need an explicit guard for snapshot-retired frames, including DELTA force overwrite. The importer must also check the latest history when a manual delete leaves no current version. [DELTA candidate query](/Users/alexcallow/Sites/frame-inventory-exercise-main/src/backend/src/main/resources/inventory-import/delta-candidates.sql:7) · [Frame service](/Users/alexcallow/Sites/frame-inventory-exercise-main/src/backend/src/main/java/com/global/ct/frameinventory/frame/FrameService.java:77)

Deploy compatible readers, filters, and guards before enabling snapshot writes. The rollout switch should be able to stop new snapshot writes while existing retirement history stays readable. Preserve DELTA replay across the migration. The current payload hash includes most frame-version columns, so adding a lineage column requires an explicit hash projection or separate lineage storage. [DELTA hash](/Users/alexcallow/Sites/frame-inventory-exercise-main/src/backend/src/main/resources/inventory-import/delta-candidates.sql:13)

### 3. Blocker — Separate committed replay from new apply

An exact replay may arrive after the 24-hour window, especially after a lost commit response. The reviewers propose returning the durable committed result to an authorized caller while applying freshness to any transaction that can write. Define the snapshot fingerprint, retained verification evidence, result visibility, and whether a failed attempt reserves the scope and capture time.

Under the exclusive lock, recheck freshness, previously committed outcomes, watermarks, and current frame state. Make the one-second lock wait retryable and the five-second apply deadline enforceable across the full transaction. Record contention, timeout, and freshness expiry as distinct outcomes. Local and DELTA writers must continue to use the same lock protocol. [Current shared inventory lock](/Users/alexcallow/Sites/frame-inventory-exercise-main/src/backend/src/main/java/com/global/ct/frameinventory/common/InventoryWriteLock.java:14)

### 4. Major — Define recovery when the guard correctly stops a job

One withdrawal in a scope with nine active frames exceeds 10%. A complete export with zero live rows also fails the draft's header-only rule. A fresh export can hit the same limits. Decide whether a signed zero-row export is valid evidence and how operators resolve a legitimate withdrawal the automatic limits block. A proposed recovery is a separate, authorized review of exact candidate IDs and current versions, with a new atomic apply. This recovery is an open decision.

A guard failure should show the eligible retirement count, pre-apply active count, and limit. A pending move should show frame ID, origin, destination, and what clears it if the destination export never arrives or is rejected. Use frame-level diagnostics for absent frames and job-level diagnostics for guards. The current row-error table requires a positive CSV row number. [Existing diagnostic schema](/Users/alexcallow/Sites/frame-inventory-exercise-main/src/backend/src/main/resources/db/migration/V3__create_inventory_import.sql:30)

### 5. Major — Make the signed evidence and validation rules precise

Specify a versioned signed format, UTC timestamp encoding, canonical scope identifiers, producer authorization for each scope, and manifest byte and event-count limits. Capture the CSV rows, expected count, and lifecycle facts consistently. A real producer needs stable frame identities across regions and a reliable lifecycle history before retirement is enabled.

Extract scope evidence independently of other validation. The current parser can stop at an invalid status before checking an invalid region. Count each malformed logical record once, and define duplicate-ID and malformed-present-plus-withdrawal behavior explicitly. [Current CSV parser](/Users/alexcallow/Sites/frame-inventory-exercise-main/src/backend/src/main/java/com/global/ct/frameinventory/inventoryimport/InventoryCsvReader.java:103)

## Alternatives weighed

- An upstream API or a second authoritative ID list can establish completeness. The signed manifest keeps the existing operator upload flow and lets the producer bind lifecycle evidence to that exact export.
- Retiring at the origin and reactivating at the destination would temporarily hide a valid frame. Waiting for an entire regional batch makes one late region delay the others. Signed move evidence allows independent regional imports.
- Automatic reinstatement based on row presence would make a stray row enough to restore a frame. A signed event provides a dated source decision and supports an unchanged returning row.
- Batched retirement would shorten individual lock holds at the cost of partial commits. The agreed single transaction keeps inventory, the job outcome, and the watermark together.

## Key decisions and staging for next steps

1. Settle per-frame event ordering, scope authority, and precedence over manual changes. Write a lifecycle decision table for move, withdraw, and reinstate.
2. Write an admission and replay table, including committed replay after expiry, a same-time conflict, and an expired or failed uncommitted attempt.
3. Decide how to handle signed empty exports and legitimate above-limit withdrawals. Define what the operator sees and how a blocked change can be resolved.
4. In GLO-33, implement compatible reads and write-path guards before enabling retirement. Verify both move arrival orders, stale broad snapshots, manual changes between staging and apply, manifest tampering, guard boundaries, apply rollback, and lost commit responses. Assert job results, frame history, and watermarks together. Benchmark the full 10,000-row workload under contention before rollout.

## Reviewer status

| Goldfish lens | Status |
| --- | --- |
| Design Critic | Completed |
| Codebase Details | Completed |
| Zoom-Out | Completed |
| Comprehension | Completed |
| Implementation Readiness | Completed |
| Structural | Completed |
| Inventive Catalyst | Completed |
EOF

content.text:
All seven Goldfish reviewers completed the [FULL_SNAPSHOT contract review](/private/tmp/glo-34-goldfish.8B6Agx/concepts_brief.md). The brief records the agreed contract and the decisions still open.

- **Order lifecycle events per frame.** A newer regional export can repeat an old withdrawal after the frame has already moved or been reinstated. The reviewers propose a signed sequence that increases per frame across regions.
- **Enforce retirement across every write path.** DELTA force overwrite, manual edits, and deletes need explicit guards so only a signed reinstatement can reopen a snapshot-retired frame.
- **Define replay and recovery.** Settle how to return a committed result after the 24-hour window and how operators resolve legitimate withdrawals that hit the 10% cap. In a scope with nine active frames, even one withdrawal exceeds that cap.

**What ordering guarantee should we require the exporter to provide for a frame across regions?**
what are the options?

| Option | What the exporter guarantees | Trade-off |
|---|---|---|
| **Increasing sequence per frame** | Each lifecycle event gets the next number for that frame. A move from A to B might be event 12, and a later withdrawal might be event 13. Every regional export carries those same numbers. | Works without a global event log. The source has to maintain the sequence across regions. |
| **Position in a shared source event log** | Every lifecycle event has a position in one authoritative change log. Regional exports carry that position. | Reuses a reliable ordering signal if the source already has one. Adds a dependency on an event log if it doesn’t. |
| **Effective time with conflicts rejected** | The exporter signs when each event took effect. The importer rejects different events for the same frame at the same time. | Requires less source infrastructure. Clock errors or timestamp ties can force operator review. |

All three need a **stable event ID** so the importer can recognize when two regional exports carry the same move. The snapshot’s capture time still orders snapshots within a scope. A fresh capture can carry a months-old event, so capture time can’t determine which lifecycle event happened last.
what do you suggest?

I’d use an **increasing sequence per frame**, assigned once by the source and shared across regions. Each signed event carries the frame ID, a stable event ID, the sequence number, and its effective UTC time. The sequence orders source events. The effective time lets the importer compare the event with manual edits.

The important detail is to track the last **applied** event. If Region A reports move 12 first, it keeps the frame active and reports that the destination is pending. Region B can still apply move 12 when its valid row arrives. Once applied, repeats have no effect, older events are skipped, and different events claiming the same sequence are rejected.
nice lets go with that

We’ll track the last **applied** source event per frame. Seeing a move in the origin export won’t consume it, so the destination export can still apply it.

The next ordering case is an overlap. Suppose a 09:00 country snapshot arrives after a 10:00 regional snapshot. The newer regional snapshot already protects that region from retirement by the older file. **What should the older country snapshot be allowed to update in that region?**
what are the options?

| Option | What the older country snapshot can do | Trade-off |
|---|---|---|
| **Skip all writes touching the newer region** | Apply changes elsewhere in the country. Skip updates, moves, withdrawals, and reinstatements if the frame’s current or proposed location is in the protected region. | The newer regional snapshot stays authoritative. Some otherwise valid rows are skipped. |
| **Allow updates to ordinary fields** | Update fields such as panel dimensions when the row passes timestamp checks. Keep location and lifecycle protected. | Preserves more changes, but creates a version that combines fields from two captures. |
| **Apply present rows under the normal rules** | Let timestamp and conflict checks decide which present rows to apply. Protect the newer region from retirement based on absence. | Closest to the original draft. A row can pass its own timestamp check and still undo newer regional evidence. |
| **Reject the whole country snapshot** | Require a fresh country export whenever any region has a newer watermark. | Simple to reason about. One newer region blocks valid work everywhere else. |
what do you suggest?

I’d **skip every write that touches the newer region**. If either the frame’s current scope or its proposed scope is protected, the older country snapshot skips the change and reports which regional snapshot took precedence. It can still apply eligible changes elsewhere in the country.

Checking both scopes matters. If Region B’s newer snapshot moved a frame from A to B, an older country export that still lists it in A must leave it in B. The regional watermark stays unchanged.
lets go for that. Makes sense

Agreed. The importer will check both the frame’s current and proposed scope and report any change skipped because of a newer regional watermark.

**How should we handle a country snapshot and a regional snapshot that have the same capture time but disagree about a frame?** That would mean two signed exports are making different claims about the same inventory at the same instant.
what are the options?

| Option | What happens when the exports disagree | Trade-off |
|---|---|---|
| **Reject the incoming snapshot** | Keep the committed result and require a fresh capture. | Matches the same-scope conflict rule. A disagreement in one region can hold up the whole country import. |
| **Skip the disputed region** | Preserve the committed result for that region and let the incoming snapshot apply eligible changes elsewhere. | Keeps unrelated work moving. The job must show what was skipped, and the first committed result stands until a fresh capture resolves it. |
| **Give the regional snapshot precedence** | Treat the narrower export as authoritative for its region, regardless of arrival order. | Gives a predictable winner. If the country snapshot applied first, the regional snapshot may need to correct changes already recorded in history. |
| **Require a shared source capture** | Accept equal-time overlap only when both exports come from the same consistent source read and agree where they overlap. | Prevents timestamp coincidence from being treated as agreement. The exporter needs a stable capture ID, and the importer needs evidence it can compare. |
what do you suggest?

I’d **reject the incoming snapshot when it overlaps a committed snapshot at the same capture time**. For the first release, apply that rule even if the two exports might agree. Their checksums cover different scopes, so comparing those checksums can’t prove that the shared rows and lifecycle events agree.

Keep the committed inventory and watermarks unchanged. Show the operator the conflicting scope, capture time, and prior job ID so they can request a fresh capture.

An exact replay of the same signed snapshot still returns its original result.
lets go for that
continue

We’ll reject equal-time overlaps and show the scope, capture time, and job ID that caused the conflict.

Next is replay after expiry. Suppose a snapshot commits, but the browser loses the response. The operator retries with the exact same signed file the next day, after the 24-hour freshness window has closed.

**What should the importer return when it can prove that the original snapshot already committed?**
what are the options?

| Option | What the operator sees | Trade-off |
|---|---|---|
| **Return the original result** | “Already applied,” with the original job ID, counts, and history link. | Makes retries work after a lost response. The app needs to retain enough evidence to recognize the exact upload. |
| **Reject the upload as expired and link to the original job** | An expiry error that also shows the snapshot already succeeded. | Keeps the upload cutoff uniform, but makes a successful operation look like a failure. |
| **Use job lookup for recovery** | The upload is rejected as expired. The operator retrieves the result through job history or lookup. | Keeps upload and lookup separate. It adds a step and assumes the operator can find the original job. |

In all three cases, the 24-hour cutoff still applies to any snapshot that hasn’t committed. Returning a stored result writes no inventory and advances no watermark.
what do you suggest?

I’d **return the original result for an exact replay**, even after 24 hours. Show “Already applied” with the original job ID, counts, and history link, subject to the caller’s permission to view that job.

Compare the signed manifest contents and CSV checksum with the durable record of the committed job. A match returns that result without writing inventory or advancing the watermark. If no matching job committed, the normal 24-hour cutoff applies.
that make sense

The next gap is recovery when the retirement guard stops a legitimate change. In a region with nine active frames, even one confirmed withdrawal exceeds the 10% cap. A fresh export would hit the same guard.

**How should an operator complete that withdrawal while keeping the automatic cap in place?**
what are the options?

| Option | How it works | Trade-off |
|---|---|---|
| **Approve one withdrawal at a time** | Show the signed withdrawal in the job results. An authorized operator confirms that frame, and the app rechecks its current version before retiring it. | Fits the one-in-nine case. Reviewing many legitimate withdrawals would be slow. |
| **Approve an exact batch** | Preview the specific frames the guard blocked. An authorized reviewer approves that list, and the app rechecks every version before applying it in one bounded transaction. | Handles larger cases. It needs an approval flow and its own limits. |
| **Use a separate maintenance operation** | Route the blocked job to an administrator who can apply the confirmed withdrawals through an audited operation with the same version checks. | Keeps the import screen simple. Recovery takes longer and depends on an administrator. |

All three preserve the automatic cap. Splitting a snapshot into smaller files wouldn’t solve the one-in-nine case, and each fragment would lose the guarantee that it covers the whole scope.
what do you suggst?

I’d choose **single-frame approval** for recovery. It handles the one-in-nine case without building a batch approval system. Show the signed withdrawal on the failed job, let an authorized operator confirm that frame, and recheck that its version and withdrawal are still current before recording the retirement.

For GLO-33, I’d keep the automatic limits and report the blocked frame IDs, the eligible retirement count, and the cap that stopped the job. The approval action can follow with deployed authorization, where we can give it a specific permission and audit who approved it.
nice lets go for that

We’ll keep the automatic cap and report the blocked withdrawals in the job results. Single-frame approval will follow with deployed authorization.

One case remains closely related. The draft rejects every header-only file, but a trusted exporter can legitimately capture an empty scope. **How should the importer handle a signed snapshot whose verified expected row count is zero?**
what are the options?

| Option | What happens with a verified zero-row snapshot | Trade-off |
|---|---|---|
| **Reject it** | Keep the current header-only rule. Inventory and the watermark stay unchanged. | Simple, but the app can’t record a legitimate empty capture. |
| **Apply the normal snapshot rules** | Accept a valid CSV header and a signed expected count of zero. Evaluate explicit withdrawals under the same retirement caps. A successful capture can advance the watermark even if no frames change. | Treats an empty scope like any other complete capture. A legitimate withdrawal can still hit the cap and require review. |
| **Record it for review only** | Show any signed withdrawals and unexplained absences in the job result. Leave inventory and the watermark unchanged. | Gives operators useful evidence while keeping empty captures out of automatic apply. It adds a separate job outcome to explain. |

A zero-row count alone doesn’t authorize retirement. We’d still require a signed withdrawal for each frame that could retire.
what do you suggest?

I’d **apply the normal snapshot rules to a verified zero-row export**. Require a valid CSV header, a trusted signature, an expected count of zero, and a checksum that matches the uploaded bytes. An empty scope is a valid observation and can advance its watermark.

Only explicit signed withdrawals can retire frames. If those withdrawals exceed the existing cap, fail the job, show the blocked frames, and leave inventory and the watermark unchanged.
nice lets go for that

A verified zero-row export will follow the normal snapshot rules, including the existing retirement caps.

The next decision is how to compare source events with manual edits. Suppose a withdrawal took effect at **09:00**, an operator edited the frame at **09:30**, and the exporter captured the snapshot at **10:00**. The edit is newer than the withdrawal but older than the snapshot.

**Which timestamp should determine whether the manual edit protects the frame from retirement?**
what are the options?

| Option | Result for the 09:30 edit | Trade-off |
|---|---|---|
| **Compare against the source event time** | The edit wins because it happened after the 09:00 withdrawal. The frame stays active and the job reports the conflict. | A fresh export can’t make an old withdrawal override a newer edit. |
| **Compare against the snapshot capture time** | The withdrawal applies because the 10:00 snapshot is newer than the edit. | Treats each capture as a fresh statement of source state. Re-exporting an old withdrawal can override an edit made after that withdrawal. |
| **Require review whenever a manual edit conflicts** | The frame stays active until someone checks the withdrawal and confirms it. | Gives operators more control, but legitimate retirements can wait even when the source event clearly came later. |

Either timestamp-based rule also needs a tie-breaker for when a manual edit and a source event have exactly the same recorded time.

# FULL_SNAPSHOT safety contract and Goldfish review

**Author** — Alex Callow  
**Date** — 2026-11-27  
**Status** — Reviewed working contract with follow-up decisions incorporated.  
**Scope** — [GLO-34](https://linear.app/upfrontbeats/issue/GLO-34/define-the-full-snapshot-safety-contract) · [Original contract reviewed](snapshot-contract.md)

## Overview

FULL_SNAPSHOT lets the app retire a frame after the source confirms its withdrawal. Operators should be able to see why it retired, which snapshot applied the change, and whether a later source event restored it. The local exercise can use a controlled exporter backed by data separate from the app inventory. A real rollout needs a producer that can make the same completeness and lifecycle claims for real inventory.

## Goals and non-goals

- Preserve one active frame and consistent version history when regional imports arrive in either order.
- Require verified source evidence for moves, withdrawals, and reinstatements. Keep unexplained absences visible for review.
- Keep apply atomic and bounded. A failed apply leaves inventory and the scope watermark unchanged.
- Keep deployed identity and permissions in [GLO-28](https://linear.app/upfrontbeats/issue/GLO-28/define-and-implement-import-authorization). GLO-34 defines the contract. [GLO-33](https://linear.app/upfrontbeats/issue/GLO-33/implement-scoped-snapshot-retirement-and-rollout-checks) implements and verifies it.

## Agreed contract

| Area | Decision |
| --- | --- |
| Export | A trusted producer reads a complete scope at a consistent point in time. Its signed manifest binds the scope, UTC capture time, expected logical row count and SHA-256 checksum to the pinned CSV bytes. The signature and evidence are checked before inventory writes. |
| Freshness and replay | Return the original result for an authorized exact committed replay, including after expiry. Compare the signed manifest contents and CSV checksum with the committed record. Reject future captures and new apply attempts older than 24 hours. Check age at manifest verification and again before apply. |
| Same-scope ordering | Reject different signed contents at the same capture time and identify the earlier committed job. A correction needs a fresh capture. |
| Overlapping scopes | Reject a narrower snapshot older than a committed ancestor. An older broad snapshot skips every write touching a newer descendant through the frame's current or proposed scope. Reject incoming snapshots that overlap a committed snapshot in a different scope at the same capture time. Report the conflicting scope, capture time, and job ID. |
| Scope and malformed data | Reject out-of-scope rows, an unverifiable required scope field, a missing recoverable frame ID, and unrecoverable parse errors. An identifiable malformed row with verified scope counts as present. More than 5% malformed logical data records fails the job. A valid header and verified signed row count of zero follow normal snapshot rules. |
| Lifecycle order | The source assigns one increasing sequence per frame across regions. Each signed event includes a stable event ID and effective UTC time. Track the newest verified event separately from the last applied event. A successful snapshot commits any newer verified evidence atomically with its outcome. Skip older events and reject different events claiming the same sequence. Repeated applied events make no additional changes. |
| Moves | A successful origin snapshot records a pending move as verified and leaves the frame active at its last known location. A destination export with the same signed event and a valid row can apply the move once and advance the applied sequence. Older events are skipped while the move is pending. Newer verified source evidence can supersede a pending move. Both arrival orders must leave the frame active at the destination with no intermediate retirement. |
| Manual precedence | Compare the event's effective time with the app's recorded time for the latest manual edit or deletion, including deletion history when no current version exists. The manual action wins if it occurred at or after the source event. Report the skip and preserve the last applied source sequence. |
| Withdrawal | Require a signed withdrawal effective by capture time. Protect newer edits or moves. Reject a live row paired with a withdrawal for the same frame. Keep unexplained absences active and report them in diagnostics. |
| Reinstatement | Require a signed reinstatement effective after the withdrawal and by capture time, plus a valid row in the destination. Matching the old frame details is allowed. |
| Retired frames | Append a RETIRED version with withdrawal and job lineage. Expose it through direct lookup, history and an explicit retired filter. Ordinary edit and delete actions reject it. Only a signed reinstatement can reopen it. The existing force rule for manual deletion remains separate. |
| Apply limits | Use one transaction. Retire at most the lesser of 100 frames or 10% of pre-apply active frames in scope. Active means a current LIVE, PENDING, MAINTENANCE, BLOCKED, or DRAFT version. Wait at most 1 second for the exclusive inventory lock and allow 5 seconds for the whole apply once acquired. Benchmark a 10,000-row import with competing writes. |
| Guard recovery | Fail above-cap jobs atomically. List blocked frame IDs, signed withdrawals, eligible retirement counts and the cap. Single-frame approval follows with deployed authorization. It will require an explicit permission, a current-version and evidence recheck, and an audit record. |

## Analysis

### 1. Review resolution — Protect a move while the destination is pending

A successful origin snapshot can verify a move before the destination snapshot can apply it. Persist the newest verified event with the successful snapshot outcome, and advance the last applied event when the matching destination row is written. A rejected or rolled-back snapshot leaves both records unchanged. A pending move stays visible until the destination applies it or newer verified evidence supersedes it.

Test Region A confirming move 12, followed by a delayed withdrawal 11, then Region B applying move 12. The withdrawal is skipped, the frame ends active in Region B, and history contains one move and zero intermediate retirements. Also test destination first and an origin snapshot that rolls back.

### 2. Implementation gate — Preserve retirement across every write path

Today DELTA compares source timestamps and payload hashes, and ordinary frame edits and deletes check the current version ID. Both paths need explicit guards for snapshot-retired frames, including DELTA force overwrite. Deploy compatible readers, filters, and guards before enabling snapshot writes. A rollout switch should stop new snapshot writes while keeping committed history readable. [DELTA candidate query](/Users/alexcallow/Sites/frame-inventory-exercise-main/src/backend/src/main/resources/inventory-import/delta-candidates.sql:7) · [Frame service](/Users/alexcallow/Sites/frame-inventory-exercise-main/src/backend/src/main/java/com/global/ct/frameinventory/frame/FrameService.java:77)

Preserve DELTA replay across the migration. The current payload hash includes most frame-version columns, so adding a lineage column requires an explicit hash projection or separate lineage storage. [DELTA hash](/Users/alexcallow/Sites/frame-inventory-exercise-main/src/backend/src/main/resources/inventory-import/delta-candidates.sql:13)

### 3. Implementation gate — Enforce atomic apply and recover committed results

Persist the verified fingerprint and result with the job and watermark. Verify that a lost response can recover the committed result after expiry. Define the handling of a failed, uncommitted attempt in the admission table. Under the exclusive lock, recheck freshness, previously committed outcomes, watermarks, and current frame state. Distinguish lock contention, apply timeout, and freshness expiry. Manual and DELTA writers must use the same lock protocol. [Current shared inventory lock](/Users/alexcallow/Sites/frame-inventory-exercise-main/src/backend/src/main/java/com/global/ct/frameinventory/common/InventoryWriteLock.java:14)

### 4. Implementation gate — Validate and explain the signed evidence

Specify the manifest version and canonical encoding, producer authorization by scope, byte and event-count limits, and how the producer captures rows and lifecycle facts consistently. The real producer needs stable frame identities and reliable lifecycle history across regions.

Extract scope evidence independently of other validation. The current parser can stop at an invalid status before checking an invalid region. Count each malformed logical record once, and capture duplicate-ID and malformed-present-plus-withdrawal behavior in the decision table. Use frame-level diagnostics for absent frames and job-level diagnostics for guards. The current row-error table requires a positive CSV row number. [CSV parser](/Users/alexcallow/Sites/frame-inventory-exercise-main/src/backend/src/main/java/com/global/ct/frameinventory/inventoryimport/InventoryCsvReader.java:103) · [Diagnostic schema](/Users/alexcallow/Sites/frame-inventory-exercise-main/src/backend/src/main/resources/db/migration/V3__create_inventory_import.sql:30)

## Alternatives weighed

- An upstream API or a second authoritative ID list can establish completeness. The signed manifest keeps the existing operator upload flow and lets the producer bind lifecycle evidence to that exact export.
- Retiring at the origin and reactivating at the destination would temporarily hide a valid frame. Waiting for an entire regional batch makes one late region delay the others. Signed move evidence allows independent regional imports.
- Automatic reinstatement based on row presence would make a stray row enough to restore a frame. A signed event provides a dated source decision and supports an unchanged returning row.
- Batched retirement would shorten individual lock holds at the cost of partial commits. The agreed single transaction keeps inventory, the job outcome, and the watermark together.

## Key decisions and staging for next steps

1. Write the GLO-34 contract with explicit lifecycle, admission, and replay decision tables. Specify manifest verification, diagnostics, and retry outcomes.
2. In GLO-33, verify both move arrival orders, a delayed withdrawal between the two regional imports, stale lifecycle evidence, protected regional writes, newer manual actions, post-expiry replay, signed empty snapshots, guard boundaries, and apply rollback. Assert job results, frame history, and watermarks together. Benchmark the full workload under contention before enabling retirement.

# Execution Instructions

This file holds bundled execution rules shared across multiple Elephant-Goldfish
Model (EGM) skills, plus drafting-only rules used strictly by `egm-draft`. Only
apply the sections referenced by the active skill.

## Plugin-Root Resource Paths

Bundled personas (`agents/<file>.md`), standards
(`resources/document_standards/<name>.md`), harness guides (`docs/*.md`), and
this file (`resources/execution_instructions.md`) sit at the plugin root, two
directories above each skill's folder (`<plugin-root>/skills/<skill-name>/`).

*   **Local / relative path**: Read `../../resources/execution_instructions.md`
    (or `<plugin-root>/<path>`).
*   **Claude Code and Cowork**: Read
    `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/resources/execution_instructions.md` (or
    `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/<path>`).
*   **Pathless `<SKILL>` injection**: If the harness injects a skill without its
    file path, check `~/.gemini/config/plugins/egm/<path>`.

Pass spawned subagents the resolved absolute paths of their persona file and
standard when `<plugin-root>` is known. A failed skill-relative lookup does not
mean the file is absent from the plugin.
Never substitute workspace files with similar names for bundled personas,
standards, or execution instructions. If you cannot read a required plugin-root
file after resolving `<plugin-root>`, say so instead of calling it missing; apply
the active skill's inline fallback only when file tools are unavailable.

## Subagent Delegation (Goldfish Isolation)

Applies to subagent-spawning skills (`egm-bootstrap`, `egm-brainstorm`,
`egm-review`, and `egm-review-loop`):

A Goldfish runs in a fresh context with no conversation history. Spawn each
subagent with your harness's subagent tool (Antigravity: `invoke_subagent`;
Claude Code: `Agent`; Codex: `spawn_agent`). Each subagent is defined in
`agents/<file>.md`, and its frontmatter `name` (for example `egm-zoom-out`) is
the subagent type to request where your harness registers named subagents.
Otherwise spawn a general-purpose subagent and tell it to read that persona
file first. Pass prompts verbatim and wait for the report. If your harness
cannot nest subagents, use direct dispatch instead of `egm-synthesizer` (see
[harnesses.md](../docs/harnesses.md)). If your harness has no subagent tool,
follow the active skill's fallback rule (`egm-bootstrap` runs scout steps
inline; `egm-review`, `egm-brainstorm`, and `egm-review-loop` stop and tell the
user that a review in the same context is not a Goldfish review).

## Shared Design & Review Constraints

Applies strictly to `egm-brainstorm`, `egm-draft`, and `egm-review` (not
`egm-bootstrap`):

*   **Artifact-First Delivery (MANDATORY)**: You are **STRICTLY FORBIDDEN** from
    presenting large proposals, drafts, summaries, or review reports directly in
    the chat pane. Write them directly to the working directory (or your
    harness's artifact directory, if one is configured) via your file-writing
    tool, share the file path or clickable link in chat, and ask the user for
    review.
*   **Plain-English Standard**: Write concepts briefs, specs, summaries,
    reports, and communications in simple, direct, jargon-free plain English.
    Explain technical mechanisms concretely. Do not summarize away substance or
    rely on buzzwords, promotional adjectives (*seamless*, *robust*,
    *blazingly fast*), or decorative adverbs (*seamlessly*, *effortlessly*,
    *literally*, *drastically*, *obviously*).
*   **Adversarial Rigor (No Sycophancy)**: Never agree by default. Stress-test
    ideas, strategies, and opinions to find weak points, edge cases, and blind
    spots before affirming anything. Lead with what is wrong, missing, or risky
    before highlighting merits. Never parrot user framing or validate asserted
    conclusions reflexively; surface what the user is missing, the strongest
    counter-argument, and whether the opposing view holds. Only agree after
    rigorous, objective scrutiny.
    *   **Banned Adjectives (No Flattery)**: Never use validating adjectives
        like `"brilliant"`, `"great"`, `"smart"`, `"correct"`, `"perfect"`,
        `"excellent"`, or `"spot-on"` on the user's inputs, corrections, or
        decisions.
    *   **Banned Apologies**: Never output polite apologies (e.g., `"I
        apologize"`, `"I am sorry"`, `"Forgive me"`) when challenged or
        corrected. State the corrected technical logic and trade-offs directly.
*   **Interaction Invariants**: Every interactive single-select gate (structured
    question tool such as `ask_question`, if your harness has one, or plain
    chat) MUST contain strictly one question (`len(questions) == 1`), set
    `is_multi_select: false`, provide clear action-oriented options without
    `(Recommended)` prefixes, never emit a structured question call with empty
    visible chat text, and be the sole tool call in its model response step
    (finish preparatory file reads or writes in an earlier step of the turn
    first, then output visible chat text and invoke the gate alone to yield).
    Ask open-ended text inputs (such as file paths or lists) in plain chat.

## Drafting-Only Execution Rules (`egm-draft` Only)

Applies **strictly** during `egm-draft` (never during `egm-bootstrap`,
`egm-review`, or other workflows):

*   **Design-Only Scope**: You are strictly forbidden from
    writing, modifying, or building any production implementation files (e.g.,
    `.h`, `.cc`, `.py`, `.go`) in the source tree. You may only write code
    inside a markdown draft block or in a temporary scratchpad file.
    *   **Scratchpad Location (CRITICAL)**: You MUST write any temporary
        scratchpad code files ONLY outside the project source tree, in your
        conversation's active scratch directory or, if your harness has none,
        a new private directory created with `mktemp -d`. If neither is
        available, keep the code in a markdown draft block. Do not use fixed,
        shared paths such as `/tmp/scratch.py`. You are STRICTLY FORBIDDEN
        from creating `.h`, `.cc`, `.py`, `.go`, or any other code files
        anywhere inside the project source tree.
    *   **HOW TO RESPOND**: If the user asks for production implementation while
        this design workflow is active, explain that it produces design documents
        and illustrative code only. Label any markdown or scratchpad example
        clearly. Do not imply that production files were changed. Ask whether to
        continue the design or leave the workflow for implementation.
*   **Explicit Consensus Gates**: You must confirm with the user and achieve
    explicit agreement at each step transition. Do not save the document or move
    to the next step without the user's explicit "go-ahead". Do not move on
    easily. Challenge the user at every step.
*   **ONE QUESTION AT A TIME (CRITICAL)**: You are strictly forbidden from
    asking more than one question in a single response. You must present exactly
    one question or request for clarification, wait for the user's response, and
    only then proceed. Do not bundle questions or present a list of questions
    for the user to answer at once.
*   **NO SUMMARIES (CRITICAL)**: You MUST NOT include a "Summary of work",
    "Status", "Adherence", or "Rule checklist" in your final response. Respond
    only with the technical content and next steps.
*   **Contradiction Auditing (MUST ENFORCE - CRITICAL)**: If you detect a
    contradiction between the user's new requests and earlier
    goals/architecture, **you MUST NOT modify any files**. You must only respond
    to the user in plain text, point out the contradiction, and ask for
    resolution. You are strictly forbidden from planning or executing any
    file-writing/editing tool in the same turn as you discover a contradiction.

# FULL_SNAPSHOT safety contract

- **Author** — Alex Callow
- **Status** — Draft
- **Date** — 2026-11-27
- **Issue** — [GLO-34](https://linear.app/upfrontbeats/issue/GLO-34/define-the-full-snapshot-safety-contract)

## Overview

A FULL_SNAPSHOT import brings the app's frame inventory into line with a signed capture of one scope from a trusted source. It can retire a frame when the source confirms a withdrawal, record a move between scopes, and restore a snapshot-retired frame when the source confirms reinstatement. Accepted changes appear in frame history with their source evidence and import job.

The local exercise uses a controlled exporter backed by inventory separate from the app's database. This lets us demonstrate actual differences between the source and the app, including a lost export, a delayed destination snapshot, and a legitimate withdrawal. A deployed rollout depends on an upstream producer that can supply the same evidence for real inventory.

## The Problem

A CSV missing three of 100 frames can look the same whether the source withdrew those frames, moved them to another region, or stopped exporting early. All three absences fit within a 10% retirement limit. A checksum can show that a file arrived intact, but the importer also needs proof that the producer read the complete scope and evidence for each lifecycle change.

Exports can arrive in either order. The origin region can report a move before the destination region does, and a recent capture can repeat a withdrawal that an even newer source event already superseded. The app must also protect manual edits and deletions while limiting the time a snapshot transaction holds up other writes.

## Goals

- Verify the producer's signature, canonical scope, UTC capture time, expected logical record count, and checksum against the pinned CSV version before inventory writes. Accept a verified zero-row capture with a valid header under the same safeguards.
- Require signed source evidence for moves, withdrawals, and reinstatements. Keep a frame active while its move waits for the destination and when its absence is unexplained. Test both arrival orders and a delayed withdrawal between them.
- Protect later source events, equal-time or later manual actions, and newer regional captures. Return the original result for an authorized exact replay, including after the freshness window. Reject conflicting same-time exports and new applies with future or more-than-24-hour-old captures.
- Preserve auditable history and direct access to retired frames. Keep snapshot-retired frames read-only until a verified reinstatement applies. Report blocked withdrawals, protected frames, and the reasons for rejection in job diagnostics.
- Apply admitted changes in one transaction with the job result and watermark. Keep the 5% malformed-row guard, cap retirements at 100 frames or 10% of pre-apply active frames in scope, whichever is lower, and enforce a 1-second inventory-lock wait and a 5-second apply deadline. Benchmark the existing 10,000-row limit under competing writes before enabling retirement.

## Non-Goals

- Deployed identity, operator permissions, and single-frame approval for guard-blocked withdrawals belong to the deployed authorization follow-up. [GLO-28](https://linear.app/upfrontbeats/issue/GLO-28/define-and-implement-import-authorization)
- The existing DELTA flow keeps its row-by-row import behavior and its force-overwrite recovery for manual deletion.
- Snapshot retirement preserves versions and history. Hard deletion and multi-scope jobs with independently named targets are outside the first release.
- This specification defines the contract. The implementation and rollout checks are tracked in [GLO-33](https://linear.app/upfrontbeats/issue/GLO-33/implement-scoped-snapshot-retirement-and-rollout-checks).

*Drafted with EGM*
EOF

# FULL_SNAPSHOT safety contract

- **Author** — Alex Callow
- **Status** — Draft
- **Date** — 2026-11-27
- **Issue** — [GLO-34](https://linear.app/upfrontbeats/issue/GLO-34/define-the-full-snapshot-safety-contract)

## Overview

A FULL_SNAPSHOT import brings the app's frame inventory into line with a signed capture of one scope from a trusted source. It can retire a frame when the source confirms a withdrawal, record a move between scopes, and restore a snapshot-retired frame when the source confirms reinstatement. Accepted changes appear in frame history with their source evidence and import job.

The local exercise uses a controlled exporter backed by inventory separate from the app's database. This lets us demonstrate actual differences between the source and the app, including a lost export, a delayed destination snapshot, and a legitimate withdrawal. A deployed rollout depends on an upstream producer that can supply the same evidence for real inventory.

## The Problem

A CSV missing three of 100 frames can look the same whether the source withdrew those frames, moved them to another region, or stopped exporting early. All three absences fit within a 10% retirement limit. A checksum can show that a file arrived intact, but the importer also needs proof that the producer read the complete scope and evidence for each lifecycle change.

Exports can arrive in either order. The origin region can report a move before the destination region does, and a recent capture can repeat a withdrawal that an even newer source event already superseded. The app must also protect manual edits and deletions while limiting the time a snapshot transaction holds up other writes.

## Goals

- Verify the producer's signature, canonical scope, UTC capture time, expected logical record count, and checksum against the pinned CSV version before inventory writes. Accept a verified zero-row capture with a valid header under the same safeguards.
- Require signed source evidence for moves, withdrawals, and reinstatements. Keep a frame active while its move waits for the destination and when its absence is unexplained. Test both arrival orders and a delayed withdrawal between them.
- Protect later source events, equal-time or later manual actions, and newer regional captures. Return the original result for an authorized exact replay, including after the freshness window. Reject conflicting same-time exports and new applies with future or more-than-24-hour-old captures.
- Preserve auditable history and direct access to retired frames. Keep snapshot-retired frames read-only until a verified reinstatement applies. Report blocked withdrawals, protected frames, and the reasons for rejection in job diagnostics.
- Apply admitted changes in one transaction with the job result and watermark. Keep the 5% malformed-row guard, cap retirements at 100 frames or 10% of pre-apply active frames in scope, whichever is lower, and enforce a 1-second inventory-lock wait and a 5-second apply deadline. Benchmark the existing 10,000-row limit under competing writes before enabling retirement.

## Non-Goals

- Deployed identity, operator permissions, and single-frame approval for guard-blocked withdrawals belong to the deployed authorization follow-up. [GLO-28](https://linear.app/upfrontbeats/issue/GLO-28/define-and-implement-import-authorization)
- The existing DELTA flow keeps its row-by-row import behavior and its force-overwrite recovery for manual deletion.
- Snapshot retirement preserves versions and history. Hard deletion and multi-scope jobs with independently named targets are outside the first release.
- This specification defines the contract. The implementation and rollout checks are tracked in [GLO-33](https://linear.app/upfrontbeats/issue/GLO-33/implement-scoped-snapshot-retirement-and-rollout-checks).

*Drafted with EGM*
### Staging and validation

Accept files up to 10 MiB and 10,000 data rows, whichever limit is reached first. Verify object size before dispatch and enforce both limits while streaming. The header does not count. Exceeding either limit fails the job before inventory writes. Keep uploaded object versions and row diagnostics for 7 days. Keep the minimal durable job outcome and import lineage available to history after diagnostics expire. Bound retries and reconciliation within the object retention period.

Interpret the CSV created_date and modified_date fields as UTC at their supplied precision. Use UTC for source_modified_at storage and explicitly interpret the existing offset-free PostgreSQL column as UTC regardless of the database session timezone. Convert source timestamps to instants for watermark and manual-edit comparisons.

The Temporal worker reads the pinned object and streams logical CSV records into job- and attempt-scoped UNLOGGED staging. Heartbeats report progress and let the worker detect cancellation. Keep the EOF completion marker in the same unlogged storage as the data. Before apply, check the marker and staged counts. If a crash leaves staging incomplete or empty, reload from S3. Store row errors with stable job, row, and error keys for retries. Track identifiable frame IDs independently of row validity. Hash canonical typed frame values with SHA-256 over a versioned, ordered encoding. Preserve meaningful text, normalize typed numeric values by value, encode null distinctly, order external references by type, and preserve the position of links. Exclude job metadata, version validity, and source timestamps from the payload hash. Compare hashes using the same encoding version. After staging, reject every row for a frame ID that appears more than once, report DUPLICATE_FRAME_ID for each duplicate row, and keep the ID in the snapshot presence set. Count each rejected logical record once toward the malformed-row threshold, even if it has several validation errors.

### Inventory and history

Use the existing frame table for stable identity and frame_version for current and historical values. Resolve region, town, postcode, and format through existing lookup tables. Attach external references and ordered links to the resulting frame version. Add job, row error, scope watermark, and import lineage storage through Flyway. Map the complete CSV to the existing model, including site and spec fields on frame_version. The BFF, protobuf service definitions, Spring service, and worker need changes for job creation, progress, and application.

Re-read the current version under the existing stable-frame lock. A newer source timestamp creates a version. Equal timestamp and hash is a no-op. Skip and report stale rows and same-timestamp collisions unless forceOverwrite is authorized and set, and record both hashes for collisions. Manual writes set source_modified_at from database statement time after locking, and CSV writes preserve the input timestamp. For existing manual versions that inherited their source timestamp, use the version’s valid_from as the effective conflict baseline. Identify those versions at migration time and preserve the original source_modified_at for history. Forced corrections record FORCED_OVERWRITE and import_job_id. Subsequent imports compare against the current version’s source timestamp, including when a forced overwrite moves that timestamp backward. For example, an 11:00 row is newer after a forced overwrite replaces a 12:00 version with a 10:00 version. Use the same database-generated boundary for closing and opening a version, strictly later than the previous valid_from.

When a frame has no current version and its latest version was closed by MANUAL_DELETE, require an authorized forceOverwrite to restore it in either import mode. Without that flag, skip the row and record MANUALLY_DELETED in the job’s row errors. With it, append a new current version, preserve the CSV source timestamp, and record FORCED_OVERWRITE and import_job_id in the apply transaction. Compare and restore under the stable-frame lock.

Promote a complete staging attempt in one transaction. Acquire the job lock and verify eligibility before writing. Use one source candidate per target key and MERGE RETURNING where it fits. Close current versions and append replacements in separate set-based statements. Commit inventory, versioned references and links, the applicable scope watermark, and job result together. If the worker loses the commit response, return the stored result when it retries.

### Snapshot apply

Keep staging outside the inventory lock. During promotion, take a shared transaction-scoped inventory lock for manual writes and DELTA and an exclusive lock for FULL_SNAPSHOT. Obtain frame locks in stable ID order. Evaluate scope membership, watermark checks, and retirement against the protected pre-apply view.

Require scope to be GLOBAL or a canonical country, country/region, or country/region/environment path. Use the explicit snapshot_as_of where available, otherwise derive it from MAX(modified_date) on the complete file. Check freshness and reject watermarks below the greatest committed value for the scope or its ancestors. A broader snapshot can still apply its present rows under the ordinary conflict rules when a descendant has a newer watermark. Protect that entire descendant subtree from retirement.

Before writing inventory, fail the entire snapshot for a header-only file, an incomplete export, or an unrecoverable CSV parse error. Also fail the snapshot if any row has no recoverable frame ID or any record is outside the declared scope. Keep job diagnostics and leave inventory and the scope watermark unchanged. Count any identifiable frame ID in the CSV as present, including when other fields are malformed. Among absent active frames, exclude protected child scopes and current versions whose valid_from or source_modified_at exceeds the export watermark. Record SKIPPED_RETIREMENT_NEWER_THAN_SNAPSHOT for the latter. If eligible retirements exceed 10% of all active frames in the declared scope, fail before inventory writes. If more than 5% of CSV rows are malformed, fail the entire snapshot before writing inventory. Keep the job diagnostics and leave the scope watermark unadvanced. Represent each accepted retirement with a new RETIRED version and MISSING_FROM_FULL_SNAPSHOT. Advance only the incoming scope watermark on a successful commit.

Exclude snapshot-retired frames from the default inventory list. Expose them through an explicit retired filter, direct lookup, and frame history.

A FULL_SNAPSHOT can reactivate an unchanged row when the current version was retired with MISSING_FROM_FULL_SNAPSHOT, the incoming export watermark is strictly later than that retirement version’s valid_from, and the row’s source timestamp and canonical payload hash match the last live version. Append a new live version in the apply transaction. Apply normal conflict rules to other rows and to DELTA imports.

## Alternatives Considered

### Forward S3 notifications through Lambda

A Lambda bridge can normalize events or route them to several destinations. The import has a single queue, and Spring Boot can consume the native event. The bridge adds a deployment and another delivery failure path.
